chapters.title: Cold Open
chapters.core_concept: Start with capability, not OpenAI announcement. An agent interacting with a desktop.
chapters.narration_summary: A computer is sitting in front of you. A browser is open. A terminal is waiting... you ask it to do it.

chapters.title: What is Astra?
chapters.core_concept: What it is, who it is for, capabilities claimed, how it differs from earlier models.
chapters.visual_sequence: AI model visualization -> browser -> terminal -> code editor -> data analysis -> professional workflow.

chapters.title: The Computer-Use Leap
chapters.core_concept: Traditional chatbot vs Agentic system. Concrete fictional demonstration: Find bug -> inspect -> run test -> observe failure -> patch -> verify.
chapters.labeling_requirement: Must be explicitly labeled as dramatized/illustrative reconstruction.

chapters.title: The Benchmark Battle
chapters.core_concept: How do we know the model is actually better? AutomationBench, ScreenSpot Pro, Agents Last Exam, FrontierMath, ARC-AGI, TerminalBench.
chapters.graphics_flow: Benchmark -> what it measures -> Astra -> previous model -> what the difference means.

chapters.title: The Scale
chapters.core_concept: 1,050,000-token context, 128,000-token max output, $10/$50 pricing. Visualized as books, codebases, logs, research.
chapters.verification_notice: Independently check against official model card before publishing.

chapters.title: Where It Becomes Useful
chapters.core_concept: Reconstruct real workflows: Software engineering, defensive cybersecurity, scientific inquiry, professional decision support.

chapters.title: The Uncomfortable Question
chapters.core_concept: Challenge launch claims: Benchmark performance vs reliability, error recovery, tool failure, human supervision, safety boundaries.

chapters.title: Ending: The Goal is the Output
chapters.core_concept: Bring it back to the central question. The paragraph is no longer the final output; the goal is the output. Cut to black.
